svg.text: Rotary Phone → Raspberry Pi Pico — Rev P (2026-08-05): original Rev K spec parts arrived -- T1 = 160G24 (19:1), Q2/Q3 = STP55NF06L (60V); centre tap RETURNS to 5V VBUS, 12V wall wart retired
Pico duties: rotary dial (WHITE=shunt/N1, BLUE=pulse/N2) → volume digit; GREEN/WHITE switchhook lever (N3) → mute; and (since Rev J) an IR-triggered ring generator for the original bell.

Audio is still handled entirely by a gutted Logitech USB headset (M/N A-00008): its own USB audio PCB (DAC + Class-D amp + mic preamp/ADC) drives a Logitech speaker + electret mic mounted inside the handset.
An internal 2-port USB hub combines the Pico (HID volume/mute) and the Logitech audio PCB (USB Audio) onto the single USB cable leaving the phone -- the PC sees two ordinary USB devices.

Rev J rationale: the bell coils measure 5.97kΩ and expect ~90V/20Hz, so they get a push-pull step-up ring generator (all switching stays at 5V). The IR pair is the trigger, wired TX+RX to the same board for bench testing.
USB HID + IR sensing + bell ring generator. Dial/hook IRQ-driven; bell serviced every loop pass. Still no audio wiring at all.
Pin.PULL_UP enabled in software (GP3, GP4 only)
named nets → panels below. BELL_A/BELL_B do NOT reach Q2/Q3 gates directly:
they drive the NEW Q5/Q6 NPN level shifters (bottom panel), ACTIVE-LOW.
under the handset cradle — GREEN/WHITE pair (N3)
USB audio subsystem (unchanged since Rev H) — gutted Logitech headset, no connection to the Pico's pins (there are none)
hidden ferrite choke in each end
Both transducers came pre-wired and pre-tuned inside
the Logitech headset -- reused as-is, just remounted
Rev J — bell (ringer) ring generator and IR trigger (named nets come from the Pico stubs above; Rev N: gates now fed via Q5/Q6, bottom panel)
IR link (emitter + bare detector, both on the Pico)
Rev N: Q4's collector supply moves 5V → 3V3 -- GP26/ADC0 is NOT 5V-tolerant.
LED4 and Q4 to cut direct crosstalk.
Bell ring generator — push-pull step-up (Rev P)
T1: mains transformer run backwards. LV = 24V C.T. as 12-0-12; HV = TWO 115V primaries in SERIES (jumper 2-3) = 230V total, 19:1 step-up.
Q2/Q3: STP55NF06L 60V logic-level (original spec, on hand). R16/R17+C9/C10 (100Ω+100nF) snubbers kept -- body-diode clamp is only ~10.7V at a 5V tap.
R12/R13 damp gate ringing. Rev N: R14/R15 now divide against Rc 1k (ON gate ≈4.5V, fully enhanced); boot-safety lives in Q5/Q6's base pull-ups.
T1 pinout (160G24): jumper 6-7 = tap; drains 5/8; HV out 1/4. DMM: R(5-8) ≈ 2x R(5-6). ~0V unloaded out = series-opposing; swap jumper 2-3.
Rev J — why these parts: the IR link and the bell drive

IR: a bare 2-leg phototransistor has no 38kHz demodulator, so ambient light is rejected by SYNCHRONOUS sampling in firmware -- read A0 with the emitter off, read it again with it on, subtract. Room light cancels.

Emitter and detector sit next to each other, so some light always leaks straight across. That resting delta is measured once at boot and the trigger sits above it, making this a reflective proximity sensor.

For the planned MCU-less remote this is the wrong receiver: synchronous detection can only see OUR OWN emitter. Swap in a 3-leg 38kHz demodulator (TSOP38238/VS1838B) then and read it as a digital input.
Bell: 5.97kΩ DC measured across RED/BLACK. At 5V that is 0.84mA. These coils expect ~90V/20Hz (~15mA), so switching harder at 5V can never work -- the missing ingredient is voltage, not current.

Q2/Q3 alternately ground the two halves of T1's 12-0-12 LV winding (tap on 5V) and the mains winding drives the bell. T1's TWO 115V primaries in series (230V): 19:1 gives ~±96V and ~15.5mA -- the original exchange spec.

Bipolar drive is required: a polarised ringer's armature is magnetically biased and must see the field reverse to swing between both gongs. Firmware never raises both gates at once (1ms deadband each half-cycle).
25Hz, not 20Hz: peak flux scales as V/f. A 5V square into the 12V half of a 50/60Hz core (160G24) is 0.93x rated flux at 25Hz (0.97x at 5.25V worst-case VBUS); 20Hz would saturate at 1.16x.

No centre tap on your transformer? Drive the whole LV winding from a 4-MOSFET H-bridge instead -- at 5V even the high-side devices can be logic-level P-channel FETs driven straight from the pins. Firmware is unchanged.
GREY pair stays exactly as found: insulated and unconnected. On many ringers it is a coil tap, and bonding it would short out part of the winding.
Part on hand is NOW the originally-specified Hammond 160G24 (dual-primary, 50/60Hz core) -- the interim 161G24 and its softer ~±48V ring are retired (Rev P).
SAFETY: the secondary swings ~±96V at ~15mA -- REAL telephone ringing voltage. Isolated from USB and limited by R18 + the 5.97k coil, but insulate it and never probe while ringing.
Switchhook (S3) behavior and firmware mapping (unchanged logic, back on GP4)
S3 is a true dry contact (DMM confirmed: ≈0Ω pressed, open released), same as BLUE. Internal Pin.PULL_UP on GP4 is sufficient; C6 100nF to GND adds EMI immunity for the long handset cord.
Lever PRESSED (handset resting) = on-hook = GP4 LOW (closed to GND) = MUTE (firmware sends a 0% volume HID report, remembering the last dialed target).
Lever RELEASED (handset lifted) = off-hook = GP4 HIGH (pulled to 3V3) = firmware restores the last dialed volume target automatically, and silences the bell if it is ringing.
Rev I summary — what changed and what's left to do

MCU swapped: Pico (RP2040/MicroPython) → Adafruit ItsyBitsy 32u4 5V 16MHz (Arduino C++). Pins remapped: SHUNT GP2→D0, PULSE GP3→D1, HOOK GP4→D7, LEDs GP14/15→D9/D10. Rail 3V3→5V (R3 pull-up now targets 5V).
NEW: LED3 “HOOK” (D11/R9 330Ω) added to indicate N3 switchhook state — lit while on-hook (handset resting, muted), off while off-hook (handset lifted).

Firmware logic ported faithfully as a POLLED (not interrupt-driven) loop -- dial/hook events are slow (10Hz pulses) so ~1ms polling has ample margin; debounce constants (15ms dial, 30ms hook) unchanged.

HID wire format changed: Arduino's HID.h requires a Report ID on custom descriptors, so reports are now 2 bytes [ReportID=1][percent] instead of 1. host/volume_daemon.py updated (VID 239a/PID 800e, reads 2 bytes).
RETAINED unchanged: dial (WHITE/BLUE, N1/N2), switchhook (GREEN/WHITE, N3), vendor usage page 0xFF00/usage 0x01, digit-to-percent mapping, and the USB audio subsystem (hub + Logitech PCB) below.
Retired: legacy_pico/ holds the old MicroPython sources (main.py, hid_consumer.py, led_blink_test.py) for reference until the new firmware is fully validated on hardware.
Dial path was validated end-to-end on hardware 2026-07-29 (dial digit → HID report → daemon → pactl). D7/HOOK was still not registering external closures at the end of that session.
Rev J/K summary — bell ringer + IR trigger added (J, 2026-07-29); bulk caps, T1 pinout, R18 derating (K, 2026-07-30). Everything from Rev I retained
NEW pins: D5 IR_TX (R10 150Ω → IR emitter LED), A0 IR_RX (phototransistor emitter follower into R11 10k), D2 BELL_A and D3 BELL_B (gate drive for the push-pull ring generator). No existing pin moved.

Firmware: rotary_volume.ino gains a non-blocking ring-generator state machine (25Hz half-cycles, 1ms deadband so both gates are never high together, 2s ring / 4s pause, 2 bursts) plus IR sampling every 25ms.

Behaviour: an IR trigger rings the bell only while ON-HOOK, and lifting the handset silences it immediately (answering the phone). A 5s lockout stops one hand-wave re-triggering. Dial/hook/HID logic untouched.

Serial test commands: r = ring, s = stop, c = recalibrate IR. New standalone sketch firmware/bell_ir_test/bell_ir_test.ino (no HID) adds continuous ring, per-gate DC continuity tests and ring-frequency tuning.

Rev K: C7+C8 (2x470uF/16V parallel, ~940uF) buffer the ~300mA/2s ring burst on the 5V rail -- prefer a SELF-POWERED hub (USB 2.0 budget is 500mA total). R18 needs only ~53mW, so a stocked 0.25W part is fine.
Adversarial review (2026-08-01, docs/revK_design_review/) fixed 3 firmware items in rotary_volume.ino / bell_ir_test.ino: DC continuity test shortened 1s->10ms (was a ~2.5A rail-short risk).

Push-pull soft-start added: first half-cycle after any idle/gap is now half-length (10ms not 20ms) -- a full 20ms first cycle from zero flux hit ~1.86x rated flux (deep saturation) at every ring start.
Ring-freq floor raised 15Hz->23Hz (below 23Hz the core saturates under a 5V square drive). Also added an AVR watchdog (WDTO_250MS) so a firmware hang can never leave a bell gate latched HIGH.

DEPENDENCY NOTE (Rev M): Q2/Q3 are now IRFZ44N (55V, on hand). 55V is under the 60V design rule, so R16/R17+C9/C10 (100Ω+10nF) RC snubbers are FITTED across each half-winding, clamping the leakage turn-off spike well below 55V.

IRFZ44N is also fully avalanche-rated (EAS 530mJ single, EAR 9.4mJ repetitive) as a backstop -- per-event leakage energy is uJ-scale, so snubber + avalanche give ample margin. See docs/revK_design_review/03_bell_failure_modes.md.

TODO: build the T1/Q2/Q3 stage and confirm ~95Vpp on the secondary BEFORE attaching RED/BLACK, then tune IR_TRIGGER_MARGIN from the live “IR delta” serial prints. The MCU-less remote stays out of scope for now.
Rev L summary — T1 corrected to the 161G24 actually on hand (2026-08-01)
Design/build were all done against a dual-primary Hammond 160G24, but the part in hand is a single-primary 161G24 (60Hz-only) -- no series-for-230V trick is possible on one winding.
Ratio drops 19:1 -> 9.6:1: expect ~±48V/~7mA, not ~±96V/~15mA. Still audible and rings the bell -- just softer than the original exchange spec.
Pin numbers changed (161G24 connection diagram): LV jumper moved 6-7->4-5, drain pins 5/8->3/6; HV side needs no jumper at all (single winding, pins 1/2).
Firmware ring-frequency floor raised 23Hz->28Hz, default 25Hz->30Hz: 161G24's 60Hz-only core needs a higher frequency than 160G24's 50/60Hz core for the same margin.
5V-side ring current drops ~300mA -> ~75mA (power ∝ ratio²), so a self-powered USB hub is no longer strictly required, though still good practice.
Upgrade path unchanged: swapping in a 160G24 or Triad VPL24-210 later restores the full ~96V/~15mA design with no firmware change -- only T1's pin wiring reverts to the Rev K numbers above.
Rev M summary — Q2/Q3 changed to the IRFZ44N on hand, with RC snubbers for safety (2026-08-01)

Q2/Q3 were spec'd as 60V logic-level FETs (STP55NF06L). The part on hand is the IRFZ44N: 55V, and NOT a true logic-level part (V_GS(th) up to 4V; R_DS(on) only rated at V_GS=10V). Both were evaluated; acceptable here.

Gate drive at 5V is fine for THIS load: at V_GS=5V the IRFZ44N still passes ~10A (Fig.3) vs our ~0.3A. R_DS(on) exceeds the 17.5mΩ rating (est. 30-60mΩ) but at 0.3A that is <20mV / <10mW -- negligible, no heatsink.

The 55V rating is the concern. The safety case: the off-FET drain is clamped to ~2xVin+0.7 ≈ 10.7V, only the leakage spike is unclamped; 55V < the 60V rule leaves less headroom there. So rather than lean on avalanche, we snub it.

NEW parts: R16/R17 (100Ω) + C9/C10 (10nF ceramic, ≥50V), one RC across each half-winding (each Q drain -> 5V centre tap). They damp the leakage ring to well under 55V. Snubber loss is <1mW at 30Hz, so any 0.25W resistor is fine.

Backstop: IRFZ44N is fully avalanche-rated (EAS 530mJ, EAR 9.4mJ repetitive) -- per-event leakage energy is only uJ-scale. So the snubber makes a sub-60V part clearly safe, and settles the repetitive-avalanche (EAR) concern.

Unchanged from Rev L: T1 = Hammond 161G24, ~±48V/~7mA secondary, 30Hz ring, all firmware timing. Only the FET part + 4 snubber parts differ. The secondary is still a real ~±48V shock: insulate it, never probe while ringing.

Firmware change is comments-only (Q2/Q3 part id + snubber note): the FETs are still switched by the same D2/D3 gate signals, so no timing, soft-start, watchdog or HID logic changes. Both sketches recompile unchanged in size.
Rev N — Q5/Q6 NPN gate-drive level shifters (NEW): 3.3V GPIO → ~5V gate swing for Q2/Q3, INVERTING (firmware drives BELL_A/BELL_B ACTIVE-LOW)
BELL_A/BELL_B (Pico stubs above) end HERE; GATE_A/GATE_B (outputs below) feed the existing R12/R13 100Ω series resistors in the bell panel. R14/R15 10k gate pulldowns stay fitted.

Why: the IRFZ44N's V_GS(th) is up to 4V, so a 3.3V GPIO can NOT reliably enhance it (the Rev M analysis assumed a 5V gate drive). Q5/Q6 convert 3.3V logic to a ~5V gate swing from the VBUS rail already feeding T1.
Inverting: GPIO HIGH → NPN ON → gate pulled LOW → FET OFF. GPIO LOW → NPN OFF → Rc pulls the gate HIGH → FET ON. Firmware (bell.py) therefore drives BELL_A/BELL_B ACTIVE-LOW (active_low=True).

Boot-safe: Rbp 10k to 5V makes a FLOATING GPIO (boot/reset, pin unconfigured) = base pulled up = NPN ON = FET OFF -- the bell can never sit energised at boot; targets the suspected ItsyBitsy failure mode.
ON-state gate voltage: Rc 1k + R12 100Ω against R14/R15 10k pulldown → gate ≈ 5V · 10k/11.1k ≈ 4.5V -- above V_GS(th) max 4V, and IRFZ44N Fig.3 shows amps of capability at 4.5V vs this ~75mA load.

Base drive check: GPIO LOW → base node = 5V · 1k/11k ≈ 0.45V < 0.7V (off, and the pin only sinks ~0.5mA). GPIO HIGH → ~2.6mA base vs ~5mA collector = forced β≈2, deeply saturated. Turn-ON via Rc ~1-2µs, trivial at 30Hz.
Values (Rb 1k, Rbp 10k, Rc 1k) bench-verified 2026-08-02 (DMM: ~5V/~0V at both gates). Any common small-signal NPN works (2N3904, 2N2222, BC547...).
Rev P: Q2/Q3 are now STP55NF06L (logic-level, Vgs(th) max 1.7V) -- shifters KEPT anyway: already built + verified, boot-safe (floating GPIO = FET OFF), and the 5V swing gives full-enhancement margin.
Rev N summary — back to the Raspberry Pi Pico (2026-08-02). Everything electrical from Rev M retained except as noted

MCU swapped back: ItsyBitsy 32u4 FAILED during bell bring-up (overheated, stopped enumerating; suspects: C7/C8 reversed polarity or D2/D3 gate-drive mishap -- never conclusively diagnosed) → Raspberry Pi Pico (RP2040, MicroPython).

Pins: SHUNT GP2, PULSE GP3, HOOK GP4 (dial/hook back to their pre-Rev-I GPIOs), LEDs GP14/GP15/GP16, BELL_A GP17, BELL_B GP18, IR_TX GP19, IR_RX GP26/ADC0. R3's pull-up returns to 3V3. Bell power stays on VBUS 5V.

NEW: Q5/Q6 NPN level shifters (panel above) -- 3.3V cannot reliably drive the IRFZ44N gates, and the user preferred on-hand parts over buying logic-level FETs. Firmware bell drive is now ACTIVE-LOW as a consequence.

IR receiver: Q4's collector supply moves 5V → 3V3. GP26/ADC0 is NOT 5V-tolerant (RP2040 ADC abs-max = IOVDD = 3.3V); the old 5V emitter follower could push it past that. Emitter LED current drops ~24mA → ~12mA.
HID wire format reverted to Pico-native: 1 raw byte [percent 0-100], no Report ID, VID:PID 2e8a:0005. host/volume_daemon.py reverted to match. Vendor usage page 0xFF00/usage 0x01 unchanged.

Firmware (repo root): main.py (IRQ dial/hook + bell.update() every loop pass, no sleep), bell.py, ir_trigger.py, hid_consumer.py, bell_ir_test.py, led_blink_test.py. Old sources: legacy_itsybitsy/, legacy_pico/.
Bell timing carried over unchanged: 30Hz default (30-40Hz clamp, 161G24 60Hz-only core), 1ms deadband, half-length soft-start first half-cycle, 2s burst / 4s gap / 2 bursts, 10ms DC-test cap.

STATUS: firmware deployed to the Pico and boots cleanly (HID enumerates, daemon connects), but NOTHING downstream of the GPIO stubs is built yet -- level-shifter values, gate waveforms, and all IR constants are UNVERIFIED on hardware.

BUILD ORDER (per docs/bell_bench_test_setup.svg discipline): wire Q5/Q6 + Q2/Q3 + T1 with the bell DISCONNECTED; DMM-check C7/C8 polarity and gate wiring BEFORE first power; confirm ~±48V on the secondary; only then attach RED/BLACK.

Then tune IR_SETTLE_US / IR_TRIGGER_MARGIN from live prints (bell_ir_test.py: ir_calibrate() / ir_monitor()) -- the placeholders are a naive 10-bit→16-bit rescale of the AVR values and WILL be wrong at 3V3/12mA drive.
SAFETY unchanged: the T1 secondary still swings ~±48V -- a genuine shock. Insulate it and never probe while ringing.
Gemini deep-research audit (2026-08-02, docs/revN_design_review/01_gemini_deep_research_audit.md) -- 4 findings changed the design before any power-on:
(1) C9/C10 10nF→100nF: the Rev M snubber analysis had a 1000x energy error and actually let the drain ring past 55V every turn-off (survivable via avalanche, but not "snubbed").
(2) MIN_RING_FREQ_HZ 28→30Hz: 28Hz saturates the core at a worst-case 5.25V USB VBUS. (3) Self-powered hub is now REQUIRED, not just preferred (940uF vs USB's ~10uF hot-plug limit).

(4) Firmware gained a lazily-armed machine.WDT (fires on a hang, never at boot -- the rp2 WDT can't be stopped, which would break mpremote) and a GP19 PADS_BANK0 12mA pad-drive fix (rp2 has no Pin(drive=)).
Rev O — external 12V ring supply (2026-08-03). Bench: chain verified at 5V (43.9Vrms at the bell, ~7mA) but the clapper only hums -- below strike threshold.
A 16-40Hz sweep (incl. sub-30Hz strike drive at the clapper's ~20Hz resonance) never struck. Force deficit, not tuning: need the original ~15mA class. Ratio fixed (9.6:1) → raise the LV rail.

ONLY CHANGE: T1 centre tap (pins 4+5) leaves VBUS and feeds from a REGULATED 12V ≥500mA wall wart (+12V EXT). Wart GND ties to Pico GND at ONE point. Rbp/Rc stay on VBUS 5V (gate swing unchanged); the Pico NEVER sees 12V on any pin.

Result: ~±115Vpk / ~18mA at the bell -- past the ~15mA original spec. Body-diode clamp rises 10.7V → ~25.4V; leakage ring rides on top -- scope the drain (IRFZ44N avalanche backstop; double C9/C10 if tight).

FIRMWARE INTERLOCK (bell.py supply-aware; SUPPLY_V in bell_ir_test.py must match hardware): tap >5.5V REFUSES plain 50% square (12V needs ≥72Hz) -- strike mode only, on-time lambda≤40mV.s: 8ms@5V, 3ms@12V.

Strike mode (new): period set by strike rate (15-40Hz; sub-30Hz now legal), gate conducts only the first on_ms; flux resets via the opposite body diode in the dead gap -- bounded by V*on_ms, not period.
USB budget RETIRED: ring current comes from the wart, not VBUS -- self-powered hub back to "preferred". C7/C8 (16V) stay as tap bulk store: fine at regulated 12V, marginal above ~13V.
PRE-POWER: (1) wart unloaded ≤13V, polarity DMM'd; (2) SUPPLY_V=12 deployed BEFORE the tap rewire; (3) wart + touches ONLY the tap rail/C7/C8; (4) dc_test('a'/'b'), then 16-28Hz strike sweep.
SAFETY: secondary now swings ~±115V peak. This is real telephone ringing voltage -- insulate the bell terminals, never probe while ringing, one hand in pocket during live measurements.
Fallback path unchanged: a dual-primary 160G24/VPL24-210 (19:1) reaches ~15mA from plain USB 5V with no external supply -- buy-a-part alternative if the wart approach displeases.
Rev P — original-spec parts arrived: 160G24 + STP55NF06L; centre tap RETURNS to 5V VBUS, 12V wall wart retired (2026-08-05)
Rev K spec parts are in hand: Hammond 160G24 (dual 115V primary, 50/60Hz core), STP55NF06L 60V logic-level FETs, and R18's original 220Ω 1W (10 on hand; it needs only ~53mW).
WHY 5V AGAIN: series primaries give 19:1, so plain VBUS reaches ~±96V/~15.5mA ideal (~13-14mA after winding DCR) -- at the original exchange spec the clapper was built for.
The 12V wart only compensated the 161G24's 9.6:1 ratio. 19:1 from 12V would hit ~±230V; 5V restores legal 25Hz full-square bipolar drive, nearest the clapper's ~20Hz resonance.
FET margin restored: STP55NF06L is 60V (back over the 60V rule), true logic-level (Vgs(th) max 1.7V), 100% avalanche-tested. Drain clamp at 5V tap ~10.7V; 100nF snubbers stay fitted.
Q5/Q6 level shifters KEPT even though 3.3V could likely drive this FET directly: already built + bench-verified, ~4.5V gate = full enhancement, and a boot-floating GPIO still means FET OFF.
FIRMWARE: SUPPLY_V 12->5 (bell_ir_test.py); bell.py floor/default 30->25Hz, lambda 40->48mV.s. Deploy ONLY once the tap is back on VBUS -- deploying early drops the 12V interlock.
USB budget returns: ~300mA LV draw during 2s rings -> self-powered hub REQUIRED again; C7/C8 940uF stay at the tap. The new T1's leads are UNVERIFIED -- full pre-power DMM protocol first.
PHASING TRAP: jumpers 6-7 (tap) and 2-3 (primaries) can each be series-OPPOSING. R(5-8) ≈ 2x R(5-6) proves the tap; ~96Vac unloaded output proves 2-3 (~0V out = swap one end).
FALLBACK if ~15mA still won't strike: 12V wart + pins 1-2 only (9.6:1) = the Rev O operating point (~±115V/~18mA, strike mode) -- keep the wart in the drawer, not the circuit.
SAFETY: ~±96V at ~15mA is genuine telephone ringing voltage. Insulate the secondary, R18 and the bell terminals; never probe while ringing; one hand in pocket for live checks.
BENCH ORDER (bell disconnected throughout, per docs/schematics/bell_bench_test_setup.svg): DMM winding ID -> jumpers -> R checks -> power -> hold() -> ~96Vac at TP-B -> only then attach RED/BLACK.
IR Audit (2026-08-07) — Gikfun EK8443 sheet reconciled against Rev P; local pair confirmed reflective-only, NOT a remote-transmitter receiver
Sheet review: 940nm emitter Vf 1.2-1.5V (2-lead); dark 2-lead receiver, rail → receiver → ADC node → 10k → GND. Sheet's 30Ω emitter is RAIL-FED/always-on, not GPIO-switched.
That rail-fed 30Ω is NOT a direct substitute for R10 -- different topology (always-on vs GP19's on/off sampling), and would need a transistor switch plus the LED's own unpublished current rating.
TX current refined: (3.3-Vf)/150 = 12.0-14.0mA ideal, ~10-13mA realistic once 12mA pad-drive VOH droop is counted. Pad DRIVE=12mA sets output STRENGTH, it is not a regulated current limit.
RX topology confirmed vs the sheet -- 5V→3V3 is the only intentional change, and it's correct: GP26/ADC0 abs-max = IOVDD = 3.3V, not 5V-tolerant.
OPEN ITEM: receiver device class (phototransistor assumed vs photodiode) is unverified -- spans ~100x in expected signal and gates every constant below.
IR_TRIGGER_MARGIN=2600 counts ≈ 131mV. A phototransistor swings volts into R11 (clears easily); a photodiode swings only mV (would never clear it).
NEW: ir_raw() in bell_ir_test.py bench-prints raw dark/lit volts (not just delta) so device class resolves from a serial log -- no DMM required.
Orientation: the sheet marks the receiver +/- (toward the sense node / toward the rail) -- confirm against the physical lead before install; reversed = SILENT near-zero signal, not damage.
CONFIRMED (matches the Rev J/K notes above): this stays a reflective proximity sensor only. It CANNOT receive an independent remote transmitter -- architecture, not a tuning gap.
Why: _read_delta() samples dark/lit/dark with GP19 forced off/on/off -- a steady remote source cancels exactly; an unsynchronized modulated source is just noise, not a decodable signal.

Side effects today: a modulated remote can occasionally cause a false-positive ring; steady bright IR/sunlight desensitizes. Future remote needs a demodulating receiver -- watch for AGC vs a continuous carrier.
